# Notice on how to resolve personal identity data errors

  * 20 March 2026
  * Government
  * Censuses / Population / Population and censuses
  * birth certificate / Civil Registration / General Department of Identification / Ministry​ of Interior

On 19 March 2025, General Department of Identification of the Ministry of Interior issued a notice on how to resolve personal identity data errors.

The notice explains that identity data errors stem from historical factors such as the loss of civil records after 1979 and manual data registration processes, as well as mistakes by officials and incorrect information provided by citizens. It outlines procedures for correcting such data, emphasizing legal verification, the principle of one identity per person, and ongoing reforms including digital systems and self-verification tools to improve accuracy and efficiency in the future.

# Operational Manual on Social Accountability Work at Municipal District and Subdistrict Level

## This document is an operational manual on social accountability work at municipal, district, and subdistrict level in Cambodia, issued by the National Committee for Sub National Democratic Development Secretariat in June 2026. It provides guidance for implementing social accountability mechanisms between service providers and citizens to improve public service delivery, transparency, accountability, inclusion, and social equity. The manual explains the background of democratic development at the sub national level, the scope and objectives of social accountability, and the roles and responsibilities of supply side actors, demand side actors, local administrations, civil society organizations, community accountability facilitators, and citizen representatives. It also covers training and capacity development, preparation of Information for Citizens posters, budget and resource allocation, data collection, performance reporting, joint accountability action planning, dissemination, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation. This document is useful for studying local governance, decentralization reform, public service accountability, citizen participation, and sub national democratic development in Cambodia.

4.6.9 
There is now a complaints mechanism built into the NCB documents. However 
the standard ICB and requests for proposal documents of the DPs do not contain 
such a mechanism for a bidder, supplier, contractor or consultant to lodge a 
complaint. Therefore the wording detailed below must be inserted into the 
bidding documents at the appropriate point in the Invitation for Bids, Bid Data 
Sheet, Bidding Data or Proposal Data Sheet as appropriate. 
“Any bidder, supplier, contractor or consultant has the right to submit a written and 
signed complaint at any stage in the procurement process. The complaint will be 
addressed to the procuring entity’s Project Manager (insert name, title and address of 
the designated  Project Manager within the procuring entity).  
The Project Manager will, first, acknowledge the receipt of the complaint by the 
complainant and, secondly, chronologically log, by date, the complaint, together with 
other complaints received.  
The Project Manager will review the complaint within ten (10) working days and 
render a written decision to the complainant.  
If the complaint is submitted during bid evaluation the procuring entity will only 
acknowledge receipt and take the merits of the complaint into consideration in the 
evaluation process. The procuring entity will respond to the complaint immediately 
after contract award. In cases of contracts subject to prior review by the DP the 
complaint, as well as the Project Manager’s proposed action or remedy, will be 
referred to the DP as part of the prior review process.  
If the complainant is not satisfied with the answer received from the Project Manager, 
the complainant has the right to lodge a written appeal within a further ten (10) 
working days, commencing from the date of the complainant’s receipt of the Project 
Manager’s response, to have the Project’s decision reviewed by the Department of 
Public Procurement (DPP), Ministry of Economy and Finance.  
The DPP will, first, acknowledge the receipt of the complaint by the complainant 
and, secondly, chronologically log, by date, the complaint, together with other 
complaints received.
